title: Credential Stuffing Defense: Quick Revision
summary: Quick revision notes on defending login endpoints against credential stuffing: how the attack works, layered throttling by IP and account, lockout trade-offs, CAPTCHA, MFA and breached password checks, ending with a cheat sheet.

chapters.title: Credential Stuffing: The Mental Model
points: Definition: credential stuffing replays username/password pairs leaked from other sites, betting on password reuse; it is not guessing, so each account gets only 1-2 tries
Brute force vs stuffing vs password spraying: brute force = many passwords on one account; spraying = a few common passwords across many accounts; stuffing = known real pairs, one per account
Why per-account lockout misses it: the attack spreads over thousands of accounts and rotating residential-proxy IPs, so no single IP or account trips a threshold
Telltale signals: high login failure ratio, many distinct usernames per IP or per device fingerprint, spikes in 401s, and a low success rate of about 0.1-2%
Defense model is layered: throttle, challenge, second factor, and block known-bad passwords; no single control is enough

chapters.title: Rate Limiting by IP and Account
points: Limit on two keys: per-IP counters stop one noisy source, per-account counters stop many IPs hitting one user; use both, since either alone is bypassed
Algorithms: fixed window is simple but allows a 2x burst at the window edge; sliding window or token bucket smooths it; store counters in Redis with INCR plus EXPIRE
Example limits: 5 failed attempts per account per 15 min and 20 failed attempts per IP per 15 min; count failures, not total requests
Behind a proxy or CDN, read the client IP from a trusted X-Forwarded-For hop only; trusting the raw header lets attackers spoof a new IP on every request
Return 429 with a Retry-After header, and keep the response and timing identical for unknown and known usernames to avoid account enumeration

chapters.title: Progressive Delays and Account Lockout
points: Progressive delay (exponential backoff): the wait doubles after each failure (1s, 2s, 4s, 8s, ... capped at about 15 min), which makes guessing slow without fully locking the user out
Hard lockout: the account is disabled after N failures until a timeout or manual reset; it is strong against single-account guessing
Lockout trade-off: it enables denial of service, because an attacker can deliberately lock out victims by submitting bad passwords
Safer pattern: soft lock by a (username, IP or device) pair, or a temporary lock that auto-expires with a CAPTCHA or email unlock; never a permanent lock
Comparison: lockout protects the account but lets an attacker lock a user out; delay stays available but is slower to deter; per-IP limits are the opposite, since they are easy to rotate around

chapters.title: CAPTCHA and Multi-Factor Authentication
points: Conditional CAPTCHA: show it only after N failures or when the risk score is high, not on every login, so normal users are not penalised
Verify the CAPTCHA token server-side with the provider's siteverify endpoint; a client-only check is trivially bypassed, and tokens are single-use and expire
Limits of CAPTCHA: solving farms and AI solvers beat it for a few cents per solve, so treat it as friction, not a security boundary
MFA ranking: phishing-resistant passkeys/WebAuthn > TOTP app > push > SMS; MFA makes a stuffed password alone useless
MFA gotchas: rate-limit the OTP step too, since a 6-digit code has only 1M values; also watch for MFA fatigue on push approvals and SIM-swap risk with SMS

chapters.title: Breached Password Checks
points: Check passwords against known breach corpora at signup, at password change, and at login, using the Have I Been Pwned Pwned Passwords API
k-anonymity: send only the first 5 hex characters of the SHA-1 hash, receive all matching suffixes, and compare locally, so the full password or hash never leaves your server
Example: GET https://api.pwnedpasswords.com/range/21BD1 returns lines in the form SUFFIX:COUNT; if your hash suffix appears, the password is breached
Policy on a hit: reject at signup or change; at login, force a reset or step-up MFA rather than silently accepting
NIST 800-63B guidance: block breached and common passwords and favour length, and drop forced periodic rotation and composition rules

chapters.title: Credential Stuffing Defense Cheat Sheet
points: Layer order: edge rate limit and bot detection, then per-IP and per-account counters, then progressive delay, then conditional CAPTCHA, then MFA, then breached password check
Defaults: 5 failures per account per 15 min, 20 per IP per 15 min, backoff 1s doubling to a 15 min cap, return 429 plus Retry-After
Lockout rule: use temporary soft locks keyed on account plus device or IP, never permanent hard locks, to avoid lockout DoS
Identical error message and timing for wrong user and wrong password: 'Invalid credentials'
Monitoring: alert on failure ratio, distinct usernames per IP, and a login success-rate drop; log failures and notify users of new-device logins
